title: Request metatag sampler and tail-latency tagger SDK
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: We lack a light-weight way to attach a small, stable set of request-level metadata to traces and metrics without paying the full cost of high-cardinality tagging or forcing full-span emission. This leads to: increased cost for tail-latency investigations, gaps in correlating partial traces for async/multiplexed requests, and noisy dashboards when teams try to add detailed tags in prod.

Goal: Implement a runtime-safe SDK API and middleware (Node/Python/Go) that emits a tiny per-request metatag (1-3 short keys) and an associated sampling hint that instructs the ingest pipeline (collector/agent) and backend to keep a small set of spans and higher-resolution metrics for the sampled requests. The system should be privacy-aware (configurable redaction), respect global sampling budgets, and add no more than 3% p99 latency overhead on typical request paths.

Design overview:
- SDK API: request.metatag.set(key, value, sensitivity=low|high, sampling_hint=static|tail-aware). The API stores a compact metatag bag (max 3 kv pairs, values < 32 chars) in the request envelope.
- Middleware: lightweight adapters for HTTP/gRPC/async workers that serialize the metatag into an opaque compact header (base64-encoded, versioned) plus a sampling_hint flag.
- Collector/ingest: sampling_hint-aware policy layer (collector side) that checks per-customer sampling budgets and uses tail-latency signals (latency thresholds, error flags) to escalate a request to retain full spans and high-cardinality metric tags.
- Privacy & redaction: SDK enforces sensitivity annotations; collector will drop or hash keys marked high-sensitivity. Admin console toggle to enforce global allow-list of keys.
- Backwards compatibility: header is versioned; fall back to normal sampling if collector doesn't understand header. SDKs default to not emitting unless explicit call in code or opt-in via environment.

Performance targets and constraints:
- Payload overhead: metatag header < 120 bytes in the common case.
- CPU/latency: <3% extra p99 for typical request (measured on sample endpoints).
- Storage: sampled retention budget should be configurable; default keep rate 0.5% of requests but escalated for tail signals up to 5% for short windows.

Migration plan:
1) Implement server SDK shims and middleware in Node + Python and feature-flag behind REDWOOD_METATAG_ENABLED.
2) Deploy collector policy changes to staging and enable in opt-in mode for internal services.
3) Run 2-week shadow mode (collector records decisions but does not change retention) and collect metrics.
4) Roll out to 10% of org traffic with observability dashboards showing sampling budget consumption and correctness.
5) Full rollout once metrics and privacy audit pass.

Acceptance criteria: see field acceptance_criteria.

Notes: design doc https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Request+Metatag+Sampler. Initial prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4862. Related: ENG-41239 (slimline context bridge), ENG-63211 (span handoff handshake).
acceptance_criteria:
1) SDKs (Node/Python) expose request.metatag.set and the middleware serializes the compact header; unit tests cover header encoding/decoding.
2) Collector accepts the header and records sampling_hint decisions in staging (shadow mode).
3) End-to-end test demonstrating that a synthetic tail-latency spike causes the collector to mark 10 sample requests and those traces appear in the UI with metatag preserved.
4) Perf test: total added p99 latency <3% on benchmark endpoint.
5) Privacy: redaction config prevents high-sensitivity keys from reaching storage in audit run.
6) Docs + migration guide published to internal observability playbook.

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: accidental high-cardinality keys creating storage blowup. Mitigation: SDK enforces max 3 keys, collector enforces coalescing and hashing for disallowed keys; admin allow-list.
Risk: header spoofing by clients. Mitigation: sign header with per-service signing key where origin is untrusted; verify at collector for public-facing endpoints.
Risk: increased p99 latency on cold paths. Mitigation: measure, add async enqueue for header emission, provide opt-out flag.
